title_en: Chongqing Deyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Reconsideration of Enforcement Ruling

full_text_en:
Chongqing Deyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Reconsideration of Enforcement Ruling

Ruling Summary

When a people's court reviews and handles a case concerning an application for refusal of enforcement of a notarized debt instrument, it shall conduct a comprehensive review of whether the content of the notarized debt instrument is indeed erroneous, including reviewing procedural issues and substantive issues. The object of substantive review shall, in principle, be limited to the notarized debt instrument itself that has been granted enforcement effect, and shall not involve the underlying facts on which the notarized debt instrument was formed.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling
(2011) ZhiFuZi No. 2

Applicant for Reconsideration (Enforcement Respondent): Chongqing Deyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 19, Gongyuan Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Wang Shide, Chairman of the Board.

Applying Enforcement Creditor: Chongqing Huaxin Asset Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 8, Jianxin North Road, Jiangbei District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Mao Huaishan, Chairman of the Board.

Enforcement Respondent: Chongqing Hengtong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 19, Gongyuan Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing.
Legal Representative: Wang Shide, Chairman of the Board.

The applicant for reconsideration, Chongqing Deyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Deyi Company), dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling No. 33 (2010) of the Chongqing High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Chongqing High Court), applied to this Court for reconsideration. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with law to review the case, and the review has now been concluded.

Facts Found by the Court

On November 24, 2003, the Heping Road Sub-branch of Chongqing Commercial Bank (hereinafter referred to as Heping Road Commercial Bank) entered into a Loan Contract with Deyi Company, stipulating that Heping Road Commercial Bank would provide a loan of RMB 189.18 million to Deyi Company for the repayment of old loans, with a loan term from November 28, 2003 to November 28, 2004. On March 20, 2008, Chongqing Guodi Asset Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guodi Company) entered into a Repayment Agreement with Deyi Company and Chongqing Hengtong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengtong Company), which stated: Deyi Company borrowed RMB 189.18 million from Heping Road Commercial Bank on November 28, 2003, and this loan was secured by Hengtong Company through a mortgage of shops on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th floors at No. 51, Minquan Road, Yuzhong District, covering a total area of 17,915.76 square meters. The above-mentioned creditor's rights and the rights (including the mortgage right) under such creditor's rights were transferred to Guodi Company, and Deyi Company and Hengtong Company had no objection to such transfer. As of March 20, 2008, Deyi Company still owed Guodi Company the principal amount of RMB 189.18 million and interest of RMB 71,698,624.29. Deyi Company voluntarily agreed to repay the principal of the creditor's rights owed to Guodi Company, being RMB 189.18 million, by July 31, 2008, with interest to be cleared upon repayment of the principal. If Deyi Company failed to repay all principal and interest within the agreed period, Hengtong Company unconditionally accepted the enforcement of the mortgage property by the people's court. On March 24, 2008, Guodi Company, Deyi Company, and Hengtong Company applied for notarization of the Repayment Agreement. On the same day, the Yuzhong Notary Public Office of Chongqing issued Notarial Certificate No. 650 (2008), granting the Repayment Agreement enforcement effect. As Deyi Company failed to perform its repayment obligations under the Repayment Agreement within the agreed period, upon application by Guodi Company, the Yuzhong Notary Public Office of Chongqing issued Enforcement Certificate No. 3535 (2008) on December 30, 2008. Guodi Company applied to the Chongqing High Court for enforcement based on the above notarial certificate and enforcement certificate, and the court docketed the case for enforcement on January 7, 2009. Subsequently, as Guodi Company transferred the creditor's rights, the Chongqing High Court, upon its application, changed Chongqing Huaxin Asset Management Co., Ltd. to be the applying enforcement creditor in this case on May 22, 2009.

During enforcement, the enforcement respondent, Deyi Company, applied on June 18, 2009 for refusal of enforcement of Enforcement Certificate No. 3535 (2008). On October 19, 2009, the Chongqing High Court issued Enforcement Ruling No. 81 (2009), dismissing its application. On August 24, 2010, Deyi Company raised an enforcement objection with the Chongqing High Court, arguing that the enforcement certificate underlying Enforcement Ruling No. 81 (2009) was indeed erroneous and that the facts were not clearly ascertained, and requested that the ruling be set aside and that enforcement of Enforcement Certificate No. 3535 (2008) be refused.

After review, the Chongqing High Court issued Ruling No. 33 (2010). The ruling held: The Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the circumstances for ruling to refuse enforcement of a notarized debt instrument are “the notarized debt instrument is indeed erroneous,” but it does not specifically specify what circumstances constitute “indeed erroneous.” “Indeed erroneous” generally includes, among others, situations where the notarized debt instrument has no content for performance, the content of performance (amount, time limit, method) agreed in the debt instrument is unclear or in dispute, the debt instrument does not clearly contain the debtor’s commitment to accept compulsory enforcement, the debtor and the creditor maliciously collude to harm the interests of others, there is sufficient evidence to overturn the notarized debt instrument, or the notarization procedure is illegal. The notarized debt instrument in this case is the Repayment Agreement entered into by Guodi Company, Deyi Company, and Hengtong Company on March 20, 2008. In this repayment agreement, the three parties confirmed the amount of principal and interest owed by Deyi Company to Guodi Company as of March 20, 2008. The repayment amount and repayment time limit agreed in the repayment agreement are specific and clear, there is a statement by the debtor expressing voluntary acceptance of compulsory enforcement, and there is no evidence to prove that the debtor’s expression of intention in signing the agreement was untrue. Therefore, the repayment agreement reflects the true intention of the three parties and does not harm the interests of others. The notarization institution’s confirmation of its authenticity and legality and the granting of enforcement effect comply with legal provisions. Deyi Company, in its objection, claimed that the notarized creditor’s right was not genuine but did not submit evidence to prove it, which is insufficient to establish that the notarized debt instrument is indeed erroneous. As for whether the Loan Contract, which is the underlying fact of the repayment agreement, involved illegal high interest or non-genuine loans, this concerns the determination of the validity of the loan contract. Whether the loan contract is void or revocable does not fall within the scope of enforcement review in this case. Therefore, Deyi Company’s objection grounds were untenable, and the court ruled to dismiss its objection.

Deyi Company applied to this Court for reconsideration of Ruling No. 33 (2010) on the following grounds

(1) Ruling No. 33 (2010) of the Chongqing High Court failed to examine whether the enforcement certificate was indeed erroneous, i.e., the authenticity and legality of the creditor’s right, which constitutes a failure to ascertain the facts clearly. The notarized debt instrument on which this case is based explicitly states that the creditor’s right arose from the principal and interest under the Loan Contract entered into between Deyi Company and Heping Road Commercial Bank. Therefore, disputes over the authenticity and legality of the creditor’s right under the Loan Contract should naturally fall within the scope of disputes concerning the notarized debt instrument. In its ruling, the Chongqing High Court listed several circumstances for examining whether a notarized debt instrument is indeed erroneous, including situations where there is a dispute over the creditor’s right. Without substantively examining whether the enforced creditor’s right involved illegal collection of high interest, whether it was genuine, or whether it was legal, nor examining whether it reflected the true intention of the parties, the Chongqing High Court directly abandoned the judicial review that should have been performed on the authenticity and legality of the creditor’s right, which constitutes a failure to ascertain the facts clearly.

(2) The Chongqing High Court intentionally evaded reviewing whether the enforced creditor’s right involved illegal collection of high interest or was legal, thereby depriving the applicant of the right to judicial relief. First, the applicant provided a large amount of detailed evidence to the Chongqing High Court proving the illegality and untruthfulness of the creditor’s right, but the Chongqing High Court only listed the defense opinions of the respondent without conducting any review, analysis, or assessment. Second, the notarized debt instrument was formed because the mortgagor, Hengtong Company, was facing asset restructuring at the time and was induced and coerced by the promise of obtaining commercial bank loans in sync with the restructuring of the mortgaged property and Hengtong Company’s assets. It was not the true intention of the applicant or Hengtong Company, nor does it meet the legal requirements for a civil act. Third, a notarized debt instrument with enforcement effect does not grant the right to appeal but only the right to raise an enforcement objection, which clearly places judicial review within the enforcement stage to ensure that any enforced creditor’s right is legal. Therefore, review during enforcement should include not only procedural review but also substantive review; otherwise, the applicant would be deprived of the right to judicial relief.

Opinion of the Court

Pursuant to Article 214 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the spirit of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether the People's Court Should Accept a Lawsuit Filed by a Party Disputing the Content of a Notarized Debt Instrument with Enforcement Effect, during enforcement proceedings, when an enforcement respondent raises a defense of refusal of enforcement, the people's court shall review whether the content of the notarized debt instrument is indeed erroneous, and such review shall include both procedural and substantive issues of the notarized debt instrument. The content of the Chongqing High Court’s ruling shows that it has, in fact, conducted a substantive review of the content of the notarized debt instrument, i.e., the Repayment Agreement, and this Court confirms that its review opinion is correct. As to whether the court’s limitation of the scope of substantive review to the notarized debt instrument, i.e., the Repayment Agreement, without addressing whether the underlying fact of the Repayment Agreement, i.e., the Loan Contract, involved illegal high interest, this Court is of the opinion that, unless issues of obvious violation of the true intention of the parties or harm to public interest or the interests of third parties are involved, it is appropriate in enforcement proceedings to limit the object of substantive review to the debt instrument itself that has been granted enforcement effect. The creditor's right under the Repayment Agreement in this case originated from the principal and interest under the Loan Contract entered into between Deyi Company and Heping Road Commercial Bank in 2003. That contract, in turn, involved repaying principal and interest from loans formed between 1997 and 1998 with new loans. Before the Repayment Agreement was signed and before enforcement proceedings commenced, Deyi Company neither raised any objection to the creditor nor sought relief from state authorities. Instead, in 2008, it confirmed the amount of principal and interest owed to Guodi Company in the Repayment Agreement and expressly stated that it would voluntarily repay. The content of the Repayment Agreement does not involve harm to public interest or the lawful rights and interests of third parties, nor is there evidence to show that it violated the true intention of Deyi Company or the guarantor. Deyi Company’s claim that the Repayment Agreement was not a true expression of intention because it was made under inducement or coercion is also unsupported by evidence and should not be sustained. Moreover, the Repayment Agreement was reached for the purpose of resolving or preventing disputes among the three parties regarding the debt and its amount, and the debtor may not raise claims based on the underlying legal relationship thereafter. Therefore, the Chongqing High Court’s decision not to review the substantive issues of the Loan Contract preceding the Repayment Agreement was not improper.

In summary, the handling opinion of the Chongqing High Court in Ruling No. 33 (2010), dismissing Deyi Company’s objection request, is not improper. The grounds for reconsideration raised by the applicant are untenable. Pursuant to Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for reconsideration by Chongqing Deyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Huang Jinlong
Acting Judge: Yu Hong
Acting Judge: Si Yanli
June 7, 2011
Clerk: Wei Dan
